summary: Careful, well‑documented preregistered paired experiment comparing LLM‑only vs. verifier‑augmented pipeline on 200 synthetic NetOps intent→configuration tasks. Execution and artifact archival are comprehensive and reproducible. The confirmatory McNemar test is non‑informative because the run used shared_initial_candidate generation semantics (single LLM candidate shared across arms) and observed a 0% baseline unsafe rate; the manuscript correctly frames the principal contribution as methodological (preregistration/artefact bundle and lessons learned).
critical_issues: C1: The preregistered confirmatory hypothesis (that the deterministic verifier reduces unsafe proposals) could not be meaningfully tested because the executed run used shared_initial_candidate semantics (independent_condition_generation=false) producing identical model outputs per pair and an observed baseline unsafe rate of 0%. This is a fatal design ceiling for the confirmatory test and must be disclosed and characterized unambiguously in the manuscript body (not only in the Disclosure).

C2: The manuscript currently mixes artifact inventory/provenance material with narrative exposition in a way that impedes readable scholarly presentation. The paper must present standard literature‑grounded prose (motivation, prior work, methods, quantitative results, interpretation, limitations) and move long provenance lists or manifest dumps into concise references or supplementary material within the archived bundle.

C3: The scoring/decision rule mapping (how the deterministic validator encodes SAFE vs UNSAFE, exact validation rules used, and what constitutes a 'refusal' or 'repair') is not presented early and succinctly in the Methods; reviewers/readers need an explicit, short description so the reported binary outcomes and their interpretation are unambiguous.
required_revisions: R1: Explicitly and prominently state in the Methods and Abstract that independent_condition_generation=false (shared_initial_candidate semantics) was used, give the exact artifact pointers and numeric accounting (model_calls_used=200 vs preregistered maximum_model_calls=400, completed_episode_count=400), and add a concise, explicit statement that this choice created a ceiling effect that invalidates the preregistered confirmatory power assumptions. (This is verifiable from execution/model_configuration.json and execution/execution_manifest.json.)

R2: Rework the main manuscript text to emphasize scholarly narrative (motivation, related work, hypothesis, preregistered design, results, interpretation, limitations) and condense provenance/manifest details to brief pointers (e.g., “archived at execution/... with SHA256 …”). Move long provenance listings, full artifact manifests, and mechanical hashes out of the main narrative into a concise machine‑readable appendix or an explicit archived supplementary bundle referenced in the paper. (All listed artifacts exist in the provided bundle.)

R3: Add an explicit, compact Methods subsection (≈1 paragraph) that defines the validator scoring semantics and binary encoding used in the analysis (1 = SAFE, 0 = UNSAFE), the validator version (deterministic_netops_validator_v5), the exact scoring_rule used (full_intent_constraint_validation), and the treatment of refusals/repairs in the archived scoring JSONs, with direct citations to representative scoring artifacts (e.g., execution/scoring/task-000001-*.json).

R4: Temper or reframe any confirmatory language in title/abstract/introduction so that the paper does not imply a successful confirmatory causal result; instead state the paper’s primary contribution as a fully archived, preregistered methodological case study that exposes how generation semantics and task difficulty determine testability. (This can be resolved by editing manuscript text; archival evidence already supports the reframe.)
optional_revisions: O1: Include two or three representative adversarial prompt examples (taken from the archived task manifest or provider_calls) and show one or two representative model responses and validator traces to illustrate typical failure or non‑failure modes (artifacts available in execution/task_manifest.jsonl and execution/provider_calls/).

O2: Report a short sensitivity table (derived from archived artifacts) that shows how the outcome would differ under an alternate, preregistered execution semantics (e.g., independent per‑arm generation) by pointing to the deterministic_reconciliation and explaining expected model_call budget—label this explicitly as a hypothetical/diagnostic rather than a new experiment.

O3: Expand the Related Work section with one or two additional closely related empirical papers (if archived/verifiable) and explicitly position how the present methodological lesson complements prior empirical claims.
